LESSON: MIDDLE DISTANCE RACES AND MONTAGE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.3: Middle Distance Races and Montage

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Middle Distance Races and Montage. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do running techniques affect performance in middle distance races?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe middle distance races in athletics
2. perform middle distance races for skill acquisition
3. discuss characteristics of a montage composition
4. create a montage composition inspired by athletes running
5. describe methods of creating a melody
6. compose a 2-bar answering phrase to a given 2-bar opening phrase
7. compose a 4-bar melody in G major
8. perform simple pieces of music in G major

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MIDDLE DISTANCE RACES AND MONTAGE
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Middle Distance Races and Montage helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MIDDLE DISTANCE RACES AND MONTAGE

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Middle Distance Races and Montage is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Middle Distance Races and Montage” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe middle distance races in athletics)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Middle Distance Races and Montage in your own words. (skill: perform middle distance races for skill acquisition)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: discuss characteristics of a montage composition)

Example 4: Show how “Middle Distance Races and Montage” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: create a montage composition inspired by athletes running)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Middle Distance Races and Montage to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe middle distance races in athletics.
3. Practise this skill: perform middle distance races for skill acquisition.
4. Practise this skill: discuss characteristics of a montage composition.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Middle Distance Races and Montage from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Middle Distance Races and Montage: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Middle Distance Races and Montage?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do running techniques affect performance in middle distance races?
2. What is the difference between montage and photomontage?
3. How can a melody be extended to make it interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Middle Distance Races and Montage means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe middle distance races in athletics.
5. Be able to: perform middle distance races for skill acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
